title: query --concept
summary: Ranked BM25 concept search over identifiers, doc-comment prose and (1.56) field captions, in the project, its repository copy and the library
intro: Read this when you know what the code does but not what it is called. It ranks symbols by how well their camelCase-split name and their doc-comment summary and remarks match your words, best first, with no re-parse needed to enable it. Since 1.56 it also searches three places (project, repository copy, library), says which place each hit came from (place, tier) and finds fields by their screen caption; see caption-concepts.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint query --concept "<words>" [--place library,project,repository] [--links N] [--limit N] [--kind k,...] [--json] --db <db>

pitfalls: approximate matched column: first 5 letters of a word stand in for porter stemming.
no synonyms and no embeddings: remove does not find delete.
exit 3 = this index has no concept-search table yet; run index once (backfills from existing rows, no re-parse).

a project index made before 1.56 prints "repository: not copied yet (index made before 1.56); run: ..."; a directory-scan index prints "repository: not copied (this index was made by a directory scan and has no project file); repository hits need a project index: `drag-lint index --project <X.dproj>`".

questions.ask: Which code does something like this, when I do not know the name?
How do I restrict concept search to classes?
Which field has this screen caption?
